blocks.heading: Basics and units
lines: Distance = speed × time. Make the units match first.
km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18. Example: 72 km/h = 20 m/s.
m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5. Example: 15 m/s = 54 km/h.

blocks.heading: Average speed
lines: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
It is not the mean of the two speeds.
Equal distances at a and b: 2ab ÷ (a + b). Example: 30 and 60 give 40.

blocks.heading: Relative speed
lines: Opposite directions: add the speeds. Same direction: subtract.
Meeting or overtaking time = gap ÷ relative speed.
Example: 14 and 16 km/h apart, 90 km gap: 90 ÷ 30 = 3 h.

blocks.heading: Trains
lines: Passing a pole or a person: distance = length of the train.
Passing a platform or another train: distance = sum of both lengths.
Example: 150 m past a pole in 10 s is 15 m/s = 54 km/h.

blocks.heading: Boats and races
lines: Downstream = boat + stream. Upstream = boat − stream.
Example: down 6, up 4 gives boat 5, stream 1.
A beats B by 100 m in 1000 m: B runs 900 m while A runs 1000 m.
